candidates.title: Québec City to Parc national de la Gaspésie by car, split at Rimouski
candidates.summary: The drive is roughly 700 km, which is too long for one 480-minute leg, so this first part runs to Rimouski along Route 20 and Route 132. The second part covers the rest. Fuel is shared between two, and a rental car is not accounted for. Access needs were not answered, so nothing here is tailored to them. This is a suggestion only and not clearance to go anywhere.

candidates.title: Rimouski to the Parc national de la Gaspésie visitor centre by car
candidates.summary: This is the second part of the drive, going along the St. Lawrence and then inland through Matane and Route 299 to the Chic-Chocs. It ends at the park's Cap-Chat side or at the Mont-Albert discovery centre, where hut check-in and weather briefings can be asked about. Duration and fuel cost depend on the exact route, which I could not verify.

candidates.summary: A cheaper option for a shoestring budget if there is no car, though services are limited and I could not confirm current routes or timings. It would likely need a transfer, and the total could exceed the 480-minute ceiling, so check it in parts. A taxi or shuttle to the park from town is also unaccounted for.

candidates.title: Park road transfer from Mont-Albert sector to Mont-Jacques-Cartier sector
candidates.summary: A short road move between the park's two main sectors, in case the hut-to-hut route starts at one trailhead and ends at the other. It avoids a long road walk or backtrack. Whether a shuttle runs, and its cost, is unknown to me. It does not require any ford or navigation in cloud, which suits the party's wish to avoid learning that on this trip.

candidatesAccepted.title: Refuge-style huts on the Mont Albert / Lac aux Américains side
candidatesAccepted.summary: Rustic backcountry huts and shelters in Parc national de la Gaspésie, matching a hut-based, demanding trip. Exact hut, route and stage lengths are not confirmed here, so check the park's current offer. Access needs were not answered and could not be accounted for. Choose marked, lower-exposure stages given no cloud navigation experience. Fords are not confirmed either.

candidatesAccepted.title: Rustic walk-in tent site near the park base
candidatesAccepted.summary: A shoestring fallback if huts are full: a rustic tent site within or near the park. It needs your own gear. Access needs were not answered and could not be accounted for. Rates and availability are unconfirmed.

candidatesAccepted.title: Mont Albert summit loop via Lac aux Américains
candidatesAccepted.summary: A demanding alpine plateau day with a good trail and views over the Chic-Chocs, suited to a 16 km limit. The trail is exposed and cloud can set in fast, so it suits a clear forecast only. Access needs were not answered and are not accounted for here.

place.name: Mont Albert, Parc national de la Gaspésie

candidatesAccepted.title: Mont Jacques-Cartier summit hike
candidatesAccepted.summary: The highest summit in the Chic-Chocs, with a marked route and a chance to see woodland caribou on the plateau. Access is regulated and guided or shuttle-based, so check current rules. The summit is exposed, so go only in clear weather, because neither of you has navigated in cloud.

candidatesAccepted.title: Lac aux Américains hut approach hike
candidatesAccepted.summary: A well-marked day hike to a glacial lake and a hut, a good way to use your hut-to-hut experience on a clearly signed trail. Cloud risk is lower than on the summits, and you can turn back easily.

candidatesAccepted.title: Chute Sainte-Anne waterfall trail
candidatesAccepted.summary: A shorter, gentler walk to a waterfall and a canyon in the park's forested valley. It makes a good low-stakes day if the weather shuts the summits.

candidatesAccepted.title: Wildlife watching at dusk near the Gîte du Mont-Albert
candidatesAccepted.summary: An easy low-cost evening watching for moose and other wildlife along the park roads and valley trails. Sightings are not guaranteed.

candidatesAccepted.title: Mont Albert plateau loop with alpine kit
candidatesAccepted.summary: Demanding alpine-tundra day on the Mont Albert plateau, which suits fair-weather hut travel but is exposed and easy to lose in cloud. Carry a waterproof shell, insulating layer, map and compass, and check conditions and trail status with SÉPAQ and the park's staff before going. Access needs were not answered, so nothing here is adjusted for them.

place.locality: Parc national de la Gaspésie, Québec

candidatesAccepted.title: Lac aux Americains cirque hut stay
candidatesAccepted.summary: A rustic hut-based option in a glacial cirque, with a demanding approach that stays within a 16 km day only if the route chosen is short. Mountain weather turns quickly, with cold nights possible even in August. Huts need booking through SÉPAQ, and I could not verify availability or the current rules. Access needs were not answered.

place.name: Lac aux Americains
place.locality: Parc national de la Gaspésie, Québec

candidatesAccepted.title: Mont Jacques-Cartier summit on a clear-weather window
candidatesAccepted.summary: Summit of the park's highest peak, reached by a marked trail in a guided or park-regulated setting, so you can avoid navigating in cloud. The summit area is a caribou-protected zone with access rules, so confirm them with the park. Plan to turn back if cloud closes in, since neither of you has navigated in cloud. Stream crossings can rise after rain, and your limit is a ford above the knee, so ask the park about water levels.

candidatesAccepted.title: SÉPAQ hut and campsite reservations, Gaspésie backcountry
candidatesAccepted.summary: Huts and backcountry sites in the Chic-Chocs are reserved through SÉPAQ and fill up for late August, so reservations decide whether the trip happens. Fees and availability are unchecked, and access needs were not answered, so I could not account for them. This is not clearance to go anywhere.

candidatesAccepted.title: Park backcountry registration and weather check
candidatesAccepted.summary: Check-in at the park's reception for current trail conditions, ford levels and cloud forecasts matters for a pair who have not navigated in cloud and rule out fords above the knee. Opening hours and requirements are unchecked, and I could not account for access needs.

candidatesAccepted.title: Offline maps, GPS and emergency beacon
candidatesAccepted.summary: Cell coverage in the high Chic-Chocs is patchy or absent, and given no cloud-navigation experience, downloaded topo maps, a charged GPS or phone and a rented or borrowed satellite messenger are worth sorting out beforehand. Rental sources and prices are unchecked, and I could not account for access needs.

candidatesAccepted.title: Travel and medical insurance with rescue cover
candidatesAccepted.summary: Backcountry evacuation in Gaspésie can be costly and provincial health cover may not include it, so check whether a policy covers hiking and helicopter rescue. Policy terms are unchecked, and I could not account for access needs or pre-existing conditions.
